interpretation.browserRowAccess: RLS enabled with no policies implies default-deny SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for the inspected anon/authenticated roles; neither bypasses RLS, owns the table or has owner/service-role membership.
interpretation.privilegedAccess: postgres owns the table and service_role bypasses RLS; this is not a claim that privileged access is blocked.
interpretation.broadGrants: Both browser roles retain broad table/column grants, including TRUNCATE and REFERENCES. Those whole-table operations are outside RLS; no execution was attempted.
interpretation.legacyMigrationDrift: supabase/migrations/20260531000000_create_beta_signups.sql creates service_role_full_access without TO service_role. Its unrestricted USING/WITH CHECK would apply to PUBLIC on a fresh application. That policy is absent in this hosted snapshot; do not replay the old definition as a security fix.
interpretation.dependencies: No direct pg_depend view references or pg_proc source/name-tracked references matched this table.

limits: Catalog metadata only; no signup rows, row counts, emails, tokens, contact/audience operations, writes, role switches, grants, policies or migrations.
No HTTP row reads, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE probes, direct database login attempts or privileged service-key access trials.

Dependency search covers direct catalog dependencies and literal beta_signups source references, not arbitrary dynamic SQL, every indirect RPC, schema exposure configuration, all role-membership paths or external integrations.

Metadata is a point-in-time snapshot; it does not establish historical access or absence of prior disclosure. Broad grants and fresh-environment migration parity remain open review items under the no-grant/policy-change constraint.
No runtime change or deployment; previous application verification remains at 1377 tests and twelve hosted checker groups. Human/content/device/retention and other release gates remain open.
The first tool-result wrapper parse selected an instructional tag mention; parsing was corrected against the stored response without re-running SQL or issuing a row query.
